newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tearful Nanjing survivor describes ordeal in court.
newsitem.headline: Tearful Nanjing survivor describes ordeal in court.

text.p: A Chinese woman who says she was raped, stabbed 37 times and left for dead during the Japanese imperial army's 1937 Rape of Nanjing wept as she told a Tokyo court on Wednesday of her ordeal and demanded compensation.
"I want the Japanese government to apologise for the massacre and to pay compensation... and I want to tell the world how terribly cruel war really is," Liu Xiuying said.
Liu, 79, is one of 10 survivors of the massacres in Nanjing who are demanding 100 million yen each ($813,000) in compensation from the Japanese government.
Nanjing, then capital of Nationalist-ruled China, was sacked by Japanese troops, who executed 300,000 people within a few months between late 1937 and early 1938, according to Chinese accounts.
Many of the victims were civilians killed in samurai-style beheadings, witnesses and historians say.
"I lost my baby in return for my life... I want people to know of the suffering...", Liu told the court, her voice choked with emotion.
She said Japanese troops tried to drag her from a basement hiding place she shared with 70 other people, she said.

"They took the men outside but the 30 women resisted, crying and shouting and holding on to doors... I was 19 years old and pregnant. I was terrified of the shame of being raped so I bit one soldier and then many others attacked me. They stabbed me 37 times and left me for dead," she said.
Liu survived but lost her child the next day. She was then taken by her father to American protestant pastor John Magee, who hid her and others in a church.
The court was shown a 20-minute videotape of footage taken by Magee in which a young Liu, covered in stab wounds, appears above the caption "Young girl attacked and raped by Japanese soldiers".
Liu described her two months of convalescence in hospital in harrowing detail.
"There were many other people with terrible wounds... many of them children and women... one young woman had been raped and then had her neck slashed wide open with a sword," she said.
The case comes amid a debate in Japan over the exclusion of Japanese wartime atrocities in school textbooks.
Japanese politicians and prominent personalities have questioned the wisdom of teaching Japan's children too much about the war, often arguing that children must grow up proud of their country.
In 1994, Shigeto Nagano was forced to resign as justice minister after telling reporters the Rape of Nanjing had never occurred.
Liu said she was angry that many Japanese still do not admit the massacre took place.
"I want to tell the world it really happened... Japanese people must tell their children the truth and let them know that war must never happen again between our two nations."

A member of the Japanese support group for the Nanjing massacre victims told a news conference it was time for Japan to face up to its past misdeeds, including forcing thousands of women -- called "comfort women" in Japanese -- into army brothels as sex slaves.
"There are very detailed explanations of the Nazi atrocities in German school textbooks," he said.
"In Japan, we have only recently agreed to give 2 million yen ($16,200) for the comfort women. It's about time the Nanjing victims were given compensation," he said.

Nanjing, in eastern China, fell to Japanese troops during the invasion of China which began in July 1937 and ended with Japan's surrender on August 15, 1945. The Chinese government says 35 million Chinese people were killed or injured by Japanese troops during the occupation.
